description:
US-004 AC5 is satisfied by equivalence (synthetic fixtures use the exact `[resolved YYYY-MM]` format the retrofit uses, and RESOLVED_MARKER_RE matches 2026-06), but no test applies the parser to the real scripts/cam/patterns.md to prove the 5 retrofitted bullets are the ones selected. A single assertion loading the real file through parsePatternsBullets/isResolved would close the gap directly.

Source: cam/issue-226
Review round: 1
Location: test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts:158

suggestion-fingerprint: 46b62a89e616

acceptanceCriteria: A new test in test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts loads the real scripts/cam/patterns.md from disk (not a synthetic fixture) and runs it through parsePatternsBullets.
The test asserts parsePatternsBullets returns a non-empty list of bullets for the real file (proving it actually parsed real content, not an empty read).

The test asserts count-equivalence between the parser's segmentation and an independent raw scan: the number of bullets for which isResolved returns true equals the number of [resolved YYYY-MM] marker occurrences found by an independent regex scan over the raw file text. This holds for any count (0, 5, or 50) and is not coupled to the current content.
The test does NOT assert a hardcoded count of resolved bullets (avoiding the CAM-245 brittleness class); it asserts the equivalence relation only.

typecheck and the full test suite pass green (the assertion currently holds at 0 resolved bullets in patterns.md, since the retrofit's 5 bullets were archived to patterns.archive.md in commit 015dbc3e).
spec.scope: Close the CAM-250 review gap durably: add one count-agnostic real-file smoke that runs parsePatternsBullets over the actual scripts/cam/patterns.md and cross-checks isResolved-selected bullets against an independent raw marker scan, proving the parser segments real content correctly. Touch only test/commands/patterns-archive.test.ts. No src change.
gotchas: The SUGGESTION's original framing ('prove the 5 retrofitted bullets are selected') is stale: those 5 resolved bullets were already archived to patterns.archive.md (commit 015dbc3e), so patterns.md now has 0 resolved markers. Do NOT assert 5 (or any fixed count) resolved bullets in patterns.md — it would fail.

isResolved(block) is literally RESOLVED_MARKER_RE.test(block) (patterns-archive.ts:156), so comparing isResolved to the same regex ON THE SAME BLOCK is tautological. The real value is testing parsePatternsBullets SEGMENTATION on real content: compare the parser's resolved-bullet count to an INDEPENDENT raw scan of the whole file text for marker occurrences.

The equivalence assertion must be count-agnostic so it stays green whether patterns.md currently has 0 resolved bullets or many; the point is the parser maps each real marker to exactly one parsed resolved bullet.

The production archive run itself (5 entries moved, commit 015dbc3e) already proved the parser works on real data; this test is ongoing regression protection against future format drift, not a re-proof of the retrofit.
